newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cancels freeze on bank loan rescheduling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cancels freeze on bank loan rescheduling.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Thursday it had withdrawn an earlier instruction to banks and financial institutions to halt rescheduling of loans until after elections set for February 3.

"In view of its adverse consequences for the loan recovery efforts, and after further consultation with the competent government authorities, it has been decided to withdraw those instructions with immediate effect," an SBP statement said.
The SBP, in a circular dated December 6, had asked all commercial banks and financial institutions to defer any request for rescheduling of loans until after the election.
It had also asked banks to submit lists by December 11 of individuals and firms that have defaulted on loan repayments or have had their loans written off since December 31, 1985.
Analysts said the move was aimed at barring defaulters, defined as those who had not repaid a loan or interest payment for 364 days from the due date, from contesting elections.
President Farooq Leghari issued an ordinance last week stipulating that candidates would have to declare that they were not loan defaulters or tax evaders.

It said candidates could be barred from standing, and winning candidates could be dismissed, if found to have given false or incorrect information. In such cases they could be jailed for five years and fined 100,000 rupees ($2,500).
Leghari dismissed Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and dissolved the National Assembly on November 5. He named a caretaker government under Meraj Khalid to supervise elections.
The SBP said in its annual report that bad debts had swollen to 113.2 billion rupees ($2.8 billion) in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June) from 101 billion rupees in 1994/95.
It said that bad debts had grown despite the recovery of about 16 billion rupees and the rescheduling or restructuring of loans worth 20 billion rupees during the year.
The SBP statement said banks and institutions had been advised to keep the central bank informed of the details of all rescheduling and restructuring of loans from now on.
